profile_text.body:
NVIDIA is a public company, traded as NVDA, founded in 1993 and headquartered in Santa Clara, California. Its most recent 10-K, for the period ending 2026-01-25, reported revenue of $215,938,000,000. On its own site the company presents itself chiefly through its Nemotron line, describing Nemotron as a family of efficient, multimodal, open AI models built for long-running, self-evolving agents, aimed at agentic reasoning in graduate-level science, advanced math, and visual understanding. The site names Bryan Catanzaro, VP of applied deep learning research at NVIDIA, as a voice behind the Nemotron vision, and cites platform support including NVIDIA RTX PRO and NVIDIA DGX Spark.

The company says Nemotron models are published with training datasets, techniques, and model weights under the NVIDIA Open Model License, which it describes as permissive and as allowing use, modification, distribution, and commercial deployment without crediting NVIDIA. The same models are also offered as NVIDIA NIM microservices, which the site says require an NVIDIA AI Enterprise license and can be tried and downloaded from build.nvidia.com. Named variants and components include Nemotron 3.5 Lightning, NeMo Switchyard for routing steps to models, Nemotron Speech models for automatic speech recognition, text-to-speech, and neural machine translation, and Nemotron Retriever models for document understanding and embeddings. The site also lists NVIDIA NeMo, NVIDIA Blueprints, NVIDIA Dynamo, and TensorRT-LLM, along with the open-source libraries SGLang and vLLM, and mentions work with partners across the ecosystem including ServiceNow.

Two products are tracked for the company: NVIDIA Nemotron, listed under chat and general LLMs with notes on synthetic data generation, GPU optimization, and self-hosted options, and NVIDIA NIM, listed under cloud AI services and model APIs with notes on inference microservices for deploying foundation models. A litigation record for the company counts 281 cases in California.
